headline: Phoenix DMV Announces 'Shade-Tastic' Summer Renewal Procedure
deck: Applicants Required to Provide Notarized Awning Diagrams to Obtain Heat-Endurance Permits
article:
The Phoenix Department of Motor Vehicles has unveiled new summer paperwork renewal rules that mandate applicants supply their own shade structures. Beginning this July, anyone seeking to renew their driver's license must complete their paperwork in twelve-minute intervals while under a personally procured shaded area.

Applicants are now required to bring a notarized awning diagram—and two witnesses to verify its efficacy—before they can even begin the paperwork process. 'This is merely a common-sense response to our scorching summers,' stated DMV spokesperson Ray Awningsworth. 'It’s the same logic we apply to sunscreen regulations, just with added paperwork and witnesses.' Forms will be printed on heat-reflective stock, conveniently doubling as emergency visors should applicants stray too far from their shade structures.

DMV staff are also tracking 'shade compliance points,' which can be traded for expedited processing times, a twist that has led citizens to form competitive shade clubs like the 'Shady Shades Alliance.' Failure to comply with shade regulations may result in a full 90-day paperwork freeze.
author: Sunny Heatwave, Senior Public Affairs Correspondent

oped.title: Awnings Over Anarchy: Why the DMV's Diagrams Save Civilization
oped.author: Horace Blister, Esquire, Grand Poobah of the Anti-Sunburn League
oped.body: In these trying times, the Phoenix DMV deserves praise for mandating notarized awning diagrams prior to issuing heat-endurance permits. Far from bureaucratic nonsense, this requirement safeguards our sun-baked society from the folly of inadequate shade. Those complaining about the process simply lack the foresight to commission proper architectural renderings, preferring instead their flimsy fedoras and pathetic pop-up tents. I, for one, submitted my blueprint weeks ago—a magnificent cantilevered structure worthy of a Roman villa—and await approval with the patience of a true patriot. The real scandal lies with shirkers who blame the heat rather than their own shoddy hat choices. Perhaps next, applicants should construct prototypes on-site, complete with wind resistance tests. Anything less invites chaos in our annual exodus to cooler climes. My own rival's hasty sketch was rightly rejected, proving the system's integrity.

stories.headline: Notary Chains Expand Awning Certification Departments for DMV Permits
stories.deck: Demand spikes as applicants submit detailed shade blueprints before summer renewals
stories.article:
Phoenix-based notary firms have added evening shifts to process the surge of heat-endurance permit applications, each requiring scaled awning diagrams signed and sealed by licensed professionals. Desert Line Certification reports processing 1,200 submissions last week alone, with most applicants attaching fabric samples and wind-load calculations.

Executives credit the DMV policy for standardizing awning specifications across three states, though one chain now charges extra for revisions after county inspectors rejected a proposed retractable shade for insufficient overlap on the vehicle hood.
